report.tagline: Microsoft's AI assistant, built into Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams and Windows, sold to companies per employee per month.
report.simpleSummary: Copilot is Microsoft's AI helper. In the office version, it sits inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams and can draft emails, summarise meetings and build slides using your work files. Companies pay about $30 per employee a month for the full version. There is also a free consumer Copilot app, similar to ChatGPT, and it is now bundled into Microsoft 365 home plans.

overview.whatItDoes: Copilot adds AI to the Microsoft tools people already use at work. It can read your emails, files, chats and meetings (only what you have access to) and use them to answer questions or create content. For consumers, the Copilot app and Windows Copilot act as a general chatbot.
howItWorks: IT buys Microsoft 365 Copilot licences per user and turns them on in the admin centre.
Employees see a Copilot button in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams.
Copilot uses Microsoft Graph, the map of a company's emails, files and meetings, to ground answers in that company's data.
Copilot Chat is free for any Microsoft 365 work user, with web answers and pay-as-you-go agents; full in-app features need the paid licence.
Copilot Studio lets companies build their own agents, for example an HR policy bot, and pay by usage.
Consumers get Copilot in Windows, Edge and the Copilot app, and Microsoft 365 Personal and Family plans now include Copilot features with a price rise.
overview.valueProposition: Save hours a week on emails, meetings and documents, inside the tools you already use, with your company's security rules intact.

businessModel.summary: Microsoft makes money from Copilot mainly by charging companies per user per month on top of their Microsoft 365 licence. It also charges for agents built in Copilot Studio by usage, and has raised the price of consumer Microsoft 365 plans that now include Copilot. Copilot also drives Azure cloud spend because it runs there.

revenueStreams.detail: $30 per user per month for enterprises; Copilot Business about $21 for small businesses.
Pay-as-you-go 'Copilot credits' for custom agents and agent use in free Copilot Chat.
Personal and Family plans raised prices when Copilot was added; Microsoft 365 Premium at about $19.99 a month for heavier AI use.
Copilot for Sales, Service and Finance bundles.
Copilot runs on Azure, so growth also feeds cloud revenue.

businessModel.pricing: Microsoft 365 Copilot: $30 per user per month (annual). Copilot Business: about $21 per user per month for firms under 300 users. Copilot Chat: free with work account. Consumer: Copilot app free; Microsoft 365 Personal and Family include Copilot; Microsoft 365 Premium about $19.99 a month.
costDrivers: GPU compute in Azure data centres to run AI models
Payments and revenue share to OpenAI for models (under the Microsoft and OpenAI deal)
Building and maintaining Copilot across dozens of apps
Sales and customer success teams helping companies adopt
Free consumer and Copilot Chat usage
businessModel.unitEconomics: One paid seat brings $360 a year. A typical office user might cost Microsoft $5 to 10 a month in compute, so a light or medium user is very profitable. A heavy user running Researcher and long meeting recaps all day could cost more. The real problem is not cost per seat, it is selling seats: only about 3 in 100 free Copilot Chat users became paid in early 2026, and many companies buy seats for only a small share of staff.

howTheyGetUsers: Existing Microsoft 365 contracts: sales teams add Copilot to renewals
Free Copilot Chat for all work users, as a try-before-you-buy
Bundling into consumer Microsoft 365 plans and Windows
Copilot key on new Windows laptops
Partners and consultancies like Accenture and Infosys selling Copilot rollouts
whatBringsUsersBack: Inbox summaries every morning in Outlook
Custom agents tied to company processes

growth.moat: Microsoft owns where office work happens: Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel, plus the company data graph behind them. A rival can build a better chatbot but cannot easily see your Teams meetings or SharePoint files. Enterprise security and existing contracts make Copilot the default choice for IT.

northStar.metric: Weekly active Copilot users per paid seat, doing at least 3 tasks
northStar.why: Paid seats only show that IT bought licences. Weekly use shows employees actually get value, which predicts renewals and expansion. A good north star metric tracks value to users, not just money. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

pmLessons: Distribution is not adoption. Being in every Office app helped sell licences, but employees still have to find it useful daily.
Pricing shapes adoption. A $30 add-on makes buyers pick a few users, which slows habit across a company.
Measure usage, not purchases. Seats sold can hide low active use and future churn.
Forcing AI into a paid plan can backfire. Consumer price rises created backlash.
Trust and data access can beat a better model. Copilot's edge is knowing your work data safely.

interviewQuestions.question: Only about 3% of free Copilot Chat users convert to paid. How would you improve that?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the funnel: aware, try, repeat use, see paid value, buy. Find drop-offs. Ideas: show what paid would have done, team trials, ROI reports. Pick a metric like conversion in 90 days.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure whether Copilot is worth $30 a month for a company?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define outcomes: time saved, faster tasks, quality. Combine usage data and surveys. Compare pilot and control groups. Turn hours saved into money.

interviewQuestions.question: Google includes Gemini in Workspace at no extra cost. How should Microsoft respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Options: bundle, lower price, prove more value, target segments. Weigh revenue loss against market share. Recommend with reasons.

interviewQuestions.question: Design Copilot features for a sales team.
interviewQuestions.hint: List sales jobs: prep calls, log notes, follow up. Map Copilot to each. Prioritise by time saved. Define success metrics like deals per rep.

interviewQuestions.question: Consumers complained when Microsoft 365 home prices rose to include Copilot. What would you have done differently?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about choice, clear value, opt-in trials and segmenting heavy versus light users. Measure churn and Copilot use after launch.
